minutes.summary: The Parks Commission heard landscape architects present two revised Marshall Park designs and took extensive public comment, mostly about the t-ball field, ball field orientation, parking and dugouts. No design was chosen; commissioners will send feedback to the designers. A commissioner also raised the failing beach house front wall, and the meeting ended with a dispute over the recreation director's absence.
minutes.headline: Parks Commission picked no Marshall Park design; most lean to option one with t-ball and basketball added.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission chose no Marshall Park design; most commissioners informally lean to option one with a t-ball field and basketball court added.
Commissioners will send their preferred option and tweaks to the designers, who aim to get feedback within a week to a week and a half.
Public comment on the two revised designs ran for a long stretch and centred on the t-ball field, ball field orientation, parking and dugouts.
The beach house front wall repair estimate left out prevailing wage and the work must go out to bid, adding time.
The next meeting is set for Tuesday March 29 at 7 p.m. on Zoom, with the beach house, lifeguard hiring and season pass rates on the agenda.

why_it_matters: Marshall Park's final design is still open, and town meeting would vote on the dollar amount, so the choice of layout shapes what residents are asked to approve.
The chair hopes to cover the project with outside money, earmarks and grants, but that funding is not secured; whatever it does not cover would fall on the town budget, mostly taxes.
The beach house wall repair costs more than first estimated once prevailing wage is added, and the season pass rates still have to be set before the beach season.
